case_slice: G04.var04 nested A OR (B AND C) versus A AND (B OR C)

parent.acceptance: accepted fixed-seed three-position one-of-three active RBD source

nested_rbd.or: G04-ROOT-OR: POS-A OR G04-SER-BC(POS-B AND POS-C)
nested_rbd.and: G04-ROOT-AND: POS-A AND G04-PAR-BC(POS-B OR POS-C)

model.repair: parent half-hour direct system CM retained; CMLocation.FMID follows FM-POS-A to FM-POS-C relocation

hypotheses_to_test_natively: The nested block references import, export and convert without error, including the leaf and subblock mode bindings.
Both arms record the same two distinct POS-B/POS-C failure samples before the scheduled mission end and before repair.
With POS-A healthy, A OR (B AND C) remains functional after both B and C fail and the long mission succeeds.
With POS-A healthy, A AND (B OR C) remains functional after the first B/C failure but aborts after the second.
Native events, report bins and repair tasks reconcile; aggregate MSUF alone does not prove the nested Boolean condition.
acceptance_gates: frozen parent/source hashes and exact structural delta; installed manual, dictionary and executable hashes
session-0 SSH with sshd ancestor, host-wide native mutex, GUI PID 13340 identity and unique run directories
native import/export/calc/report and exact authored-row roundtrip with zero converter errors
author event and ledger replay plus independent read-only review on raw evidence
raw invocation, logs, model, report and closure files sealed by SHA-256 evidence index
limits: One fixed seed and a nonfailing POS-A distinguish only one observed failure combination, not a full truth table or population reliability.
This pair does not test A failure, alternate failure orders, same-time failures, QTYPB>1, nested passive switching, GUI RBD view or cross-engine parity.
